title: Complaint in Adversary Proceeding for Fraudulent Transfer and Avoidance of Preferential Payments
text:
UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
HOUSTON DIVISION

In re: Mark A. Delgado, Debtor.

Case No. 24-31892 (Chapter 7)

Adversary Proceeding No. 24-04071

Crescent Financial Partners, LLC, Plaintiff,
v.

Delgado Holdings, Inc., Defendant.

CAUSE NO. 24-04071

COMPLAINT SEEKING AVOIDANCE OF FRAUDULENT TRANSFER, TURNOVER, AND DAMAGES

COMES NOW Plaintiff Crescent Financial Partners, LLC, a Texas limited liability company with principal offices at 4520 Westheimer Road, Suite 200, Houston, Texas 77027, and files this Complaint against Defendant Delgado Holdings, Inc., alleging as follows:

I. PARTIES
1. Plaintiff Crescent Financial Partners, LLC (“Crescent”) is a creditor of the bankruptcy estate of Mark A. Delgado, Debtor, holding an unsecured claim in the amount of $1,247,500.00, as evidenced by a promissory note executed on June 3, 2021.
2. Defendant Delgado Holdings, Inc. (“Delgado Holdings”) is a Texas corporation with its registered office at 2211 San Felipe Street, Suite 400, Houston, Texas 77019. Delgado Holdings was formerly known as Delgado Industries, Inc. and is an entity controlled by Debtor Mark A. Delgado.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE
3. This Court has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. §§ 157 and 1334. This is a core proceeding under 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(H) (fraudulent transfer) and (F) (preferential transfer). Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1409.
4. This adversary proceeding is brought pursuant to 11 U.S.C. § 548 and Texas Business & Commerce Code § 24.005(a)(1).

III. FACTUAL BACKGROUND
5. On January 15, 2024, Mark A. Delgado (born on March 14, 1971) filed a voluntary petition under Chapter 7 of the Bankruptcy Code. The Debtor’s Social Security Number is 458-12-8897. The case was assigned to Judge Whitfield.
6. Prior to bankruptcy, Debtor transferred $875,000.00 to Delgado Holdings on November 20, 2023, without receiving reasonably equivalent value. At the time of transfer, Debtor was insolvent or became insolvent as a result.
7. Additionally, on December 5, 2023, Delgado Holdings received $120,000.00 from Debtor to satisfy a pre-existing debt owed by Debtor to Delgado Holdings, within 90 days of the petition date, constituting a preferential transfer under 11 U.S.C. § 547.
8. Delgado Holdings continues to hold the funds in its corporate checking account at Texas Commerce Bank, account number 8842-9910-3387.

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION
COUNT ONE – Fraudulent Transfer (11 U.S.C. § 548)
9. Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-8. The transfer to Delgado Holdings was made with actual intent to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors, or constructively fraudulent because Debtor received less than reasonably equivalent value. See In re Sunbelt Grain & Feed, Inc., 406 B.R. 358 (Bankr. N.D. Tex. 2009).

COUNT TWO – Preferential Transfer (11 U.S.C. § 547)
10. Plaintiff incorporates paragraphs 1-8. The $120,000.00 payment to Delgado Holdings is avoidable as a preference, and Plaintiff seeks recovery under 11 U.S.C. § 550(a)(1).

COUNT THREE – Avoidance Under Texas Law
11. In the alternative, the transfer is voidable under Texas Business & Commerce Code § 24.005(a)(1).

V. DEMAND FOR TURNOVER AND RELIEF
12. Plaintiff demands judgment against Delgado Holdings for $995,000.00, plus interest, costs, and such other relief as the Court deems just.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that the Court: (a) avoid the transfers; (b) enter judgment for $995,000.00; (c) order turnover of the funds or their value; and (d) grant such other relief.

DATED: June 10, 2024.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Elena M. Vasquez
Elena M. Vasquez

Houston, Texas 77002
Phone: (713) 555-2468

ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

title: Adversary Complaint to Determine Dischargeability of Debt Under 11 U.S.C. § 523(a)(2)(A)
text:
UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
DALLAS DIVISION

In re: Charles Timothy Whitaker, Debtor.

Bankruptcy Case No. 24-04182

Adversary Proceeding No. 24-03012

Phoenix Medical Supply, Inc., Plaintiff,
v.

Charles Timothy Whitaker, Defendant.

CAUSE NO. 24-03012

COMPLAINT TO DETERMINE DISCHARGEABILITY OF DEBT (FRAUD)

Phoenix Medical Supply, Inc. (“Phoenix”) files this Complaint against Defendant Charles Timothy Whitaker, seeking a determination that the debt owed is non-dischargeable.

I. PARTIES
1. Plaintiff Phoenix Medical Supply, Inc. is a Texas corporation with its principal place of business at 3100 McKinney Avenue, Suite 520, Dallas, Texas 75204.
2. Defendant Charles Timothy Whitaker is an individual residing at 7423 Elm Street, Dallas, Texas 75225. Defendant’s Social Security Number is 512-88-4421.

II. JURISDICTION
3. This Court has jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1334(b) and 11 U.S.C. § 523(a). Venue is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1409(a).

III. FACTS
4. Between January and March 2023, Defendant Whitaker, as CEO of Whitaker Health Group, LLC, induced Phoenix to supply $450,000.00 of medical devices by representing that payment would be made within 30 days. Whitaker Health Group, LLC is a Texas limited liability company formerly known as Whitaker Medical Services, LLC.
5. Defendant Whitaker never intended to pay. He used the devices for personal resale and dissipated the proceeds. Phoenix discovered the fraud on April 1, 2023, and obtained a state court judgment against Defendant on August 12, 2023 (cause number DC-23-08971 in the 162nd District Court of Dallas County).
6. Defendant filed bankruptcy on January 5, 2024. The debt owed to Phoenix is $450,000.00 plus interest.
7. Defendant’s spouse is Rachel Whitaker (née Sandoval). A minor child, A.B., resides in the household.

IV. CAUSE OF ACTION – NON-DISCHARGEABILITY
8. The debt is non-dischargeable under 11 U.S.C. § 523(a)(2)(A) as a debt for money obtained by false pretenses, false representation, or actual fraud. Defendant made material misrepresentations with intent to deceive, Phoenix reasonably relied, and suffered loss.

V. RELIEF
9. Phoenix requests judgment that the debt is non-dischargeable, with costs and attorney’s fees under 11 U.S.C. § 523(d).

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Marcus J. Delaney
Marcus J. Delaney
Texas Bar No. 24099123
Delaney & Pratt, LLP

Dallas, Texas 75201
Phone: (214) 555-3399
Email: mdelaney@delaneypratt.com
ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

/s/ Marcus J. Delaney

title: Adversary Complaint for Objection to Discharge and Turnover of Estate Property
text:
UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE WESTERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
AUSTIN DIVISION

In re: Deborah Lynn Callahan, Debtor.

Case No. 24-05678

Adversary Proceeding No. 24-05009

Harold J. Thurgood, Trustee, Plaintiff,
v.

Callahan Real Estate Ventures, LLC, Defendant.

CAUSE NO. 24-05009

COMPLAINT OBJECTING TO DISCHARGE AND FOR TURNOVER

Harold J. Thurgood, the Chapter 7 Trustee of the estate of Deborah Lynn Callahan, brings this adversary proceeding against Callahan Real Estate Ventures, LLC.

I. PARTIES
1. Plaintiff Harold J. Thurgood is the duly appointed Chapter 7 Trustee in the above-captioned case.
2. Defendant Callahan Real Estate Ventures, LLC is a Texas limited liability company with offices at 901 Congress Avenue, Austin, Texas 78701.
3. Debtor Deborah Lynn Callahan resides at 512 Barton Creek Boulevard, Austin, Texas 78746. Debtor’s date of birth is March 14, 1971. Debtor’s SSN is 361-77-2045.

II. PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND
4. Debtor filed for relief under Chapter 7 on February 20, 2024. The meeting of creditors was held on April 3, 2024, and was continued to April 17, 2024.
5. On April 17, 2024, Debtor refused to answer questions regarding the transfer of $300,000.00 to Callahan Real Estate Ventures, LLC, made on December 15, 2023.

III. CAUSES OF ACTION
COUNT I – Objection to Discharge (11 U.S.C. § 727(a)(6)(A))
6. Debtor refused to obey a lawful order of the Court, specifically Judge Okafor’s order compelling answers. Therefore, discharge should be denied.

COUNT II – Turnover (11 U.S.C. § 542(a))
7. Defendant holds $300,000.00 that is property of the estate. Plaintiff demands turnover.

IV. FACTS REGARDING TRANSFER
8. The transfer was made to Callahan Real Estate Ventures, LLC, an entity wholly owned by Debtor’s brother, Robert J. Callahan. No consideration was given. The transfer was made within one year of filing and while Debtor was insolvent.

V. RELIEF
9. Plaintiff seeks denial of discharge and judgment for $300,000.00.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Anita R. Fernandez
Anita R. Fernandez
Texas Bar No. 24081812
Fernandez & Kim, LLP
1000 Guadalupe Street, Austin, Texas 78705
Phone: (512) 555-1011
Email: afernandez@fernandezkim.com
ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I served this Complaint on Defendant via certified mail to its registered agent.

DATED: May 1, 2024

title: Adversary Complaint to Recover Avoidable Intercompany Transfers and for Substantive Consolidation
text:
UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
TYLER DIVISION

In re: Grandview Operating, LLC, Debtor.

Case No. 24-60123

Adversary Proceeding No. 24-06077

R. Michael Tanner, Trustee, Plaintiff,
v.

Grandview Energy Holdings, Inc., Defendant.

CAUSE NO. 24-06077

COMPLAINT FOR AVOIDANCE AND RECOVERY OF TRANSFERS, AND FOR SUBSTANTIVE CONSOLIDATION

R. Michael Tanner, Trustee of the estate of Grandview Operating, LLC, files this Complaint.

I. PARTIES
1. Plaintiff R. Michael Tanner is the Chapter 7 Trustee. His address is 2000 Heritage Drive, Tyler, Texas 75701.
2. Defendant Grandview Energy Holdings, Inc. is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 44 Corporate Park, Tyler, Texas 75702.
3. Debtor Grandview Operating, LLC’s sole member is Defendant Grandview Energy Holdings, Inc. The Debtor operated oil and gas properties in east Texas.

II. JURISDICTION
4. This Court has jurisdiction pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1334(b) and the Standing Order of Reference. This is a core proceeding under 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(H).

III. FACTS
5. Debtor filed for bankruptcy on January 30, 2024. Debtor’s officers included James R. Hale (CEO), Sandra M. Pruitt (CFO), and minor shareholder A.B. (a minor who is the child of Hale).
6. Between November 2023 and January 2024, Debtor transferred $2,400,000.00 to Defendant, described as “management fees.” No services were provided. Those transfers were made while Debtor was insolvent.
7. Defendant commingled assets with Debtor, maintained no separate books, and used Debtor’s funds for Defendant’s obligations. Substantive consolidation is appropriate.
8. Debtor’s SSN (EIN) is 75-1849932. Defendant’s EIN is 75-3320410.

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION
COUNT I – Fraudulent Transfer (11 U.S.C. § 548(a)(1)(B))
9. The transfers were constructively fraudulent because Debtor received less than reasonably equivalent value and was insolvent. See In re TransTexas Gas Corp., 597 F.3d 298 (5th Cir. 2010).

COUNT II – Substantive Consolidation
10. The entities should be substantively consolidated under the Court’s equitable powers. See In re Gandy, 299 B.R. 782 (Bankr. N.D. Tex. 2003).

COUNT III – Turnover
11. Defendant is in possession of estate property and must turn it over under 11 U.S.C. § 542.

V. RELIEF
12. Plaintiff requests judgment for $2,400,000.00, substantive consolidation, and costs.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Peter J. Kowalski
Peter J. Kowalski
Texas Bar No. 24010445
Kowalski Barnes LLP

Phone: (903) 555-7788
Email: pkowalski@kowalskibarnes.com
ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
I certify that I served this Complaint on Defendant via ECF on June 15, 2024.

/s/ Peter J. Kowalski

title: Adversary Complaint for Revocation of Discharge and Recovery of Attorney Fees
text:
UNITED STATES BANKRUPTCY COURT FOR THE SOUTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
CORPUS CHRISTI DIVISION

In re: Patricia Ann Holloway, Debtor.

Case No. 24-22109

Adversary Proceeding No. 24-07023

Coastal Savings Bank, Plaintiff,
v.

Patricia Ann Holloway, Defendant.

CAUSE NO. 24-07023

COMPLAINT TO REVOKE DISCHARGE AND RECOVER ATTORNEY’S FEES

Coastal Savings Bank (“Coastal”) brings this adversary complaint against Patricia Ann Holloway.

I. PARTIES
1. Plaintiff Coastal Savings Bank is a federally insured bank with its headquarters at 5500 Ocean Drive, Corpus Christi, Texas 78411.
2. Defendant Patricia Ann Holloway is an individual residing at 88 Harbor Lane, Corpus Christi, Texas 78402. Defendant is also known as Patricia Ann Reyes (her maiden name) and formerly known as Patricia Holloway-Peterson.
3. Defendant’s date of birth is March 14, 1971, and her SSN is 460-55-8712.

II. JURISDICTION
4. Jurisdiction is proper under 28 U.S.C. § 1334(b). This is a core proceeding under 28 U.S.C. § 157(b)(2)(J) (revocation of discharge).

III. FACTS
5. Defendant filed Chapter 7 on October 1, 2023. Discharge was entered on January 15, 2024.
6. Before filing, Defendant obtained a loan from Coastal in the amount of $300,000.00, on June 1, 2023, by submitting falsified financial statements. She also transferred $50,000.00 to her brother, Carlos D. Reyes, on December 20, 2023, with intent to hinder creditors.
7. Defendant’s discharge was obtained through fraud; she deliberately concealed her interest in a boat, worth $75,000.00.
8. Coastal seeks revocation of discharge under 11 U.S.C. § 727(d)(1) and recovery of attorney’s fees under § 727(e).

IV. CAUSE OF ACTION
9. Defendant fraudulently concealed assets and made false oaths. The discharge should be revoked.

V. RELIEF
10. Plaintiff requests revocation of discharge, judgment for $300,000.00, fees, and costs.

Respectfully submitted,

/s/ Laura K. Simmons

ATTORNEY FOR PLAINTIFF

/s/ Laura K. Simmons
